(2) Cannabis banking and payment processing providers (PayQwick, Hypur, CanPay digital payment solutions, Safe Harbor Financial for banking, Dama Financial, Green Check Verified, POSaBIT cashless payments, Aeropay, SpringBig integrated payments and loyalty) solving the cannabis industry's cash-intensive operations problem due to federal banking restrictions under the Controlled Substances Act — payment processors charge 3-8% per transaction plus monthly fees, generating $15,000-$100,000/year in revenue per dispensary customer depending on transaction volume, making payment providers willing to pay $8,000-$15,000/year for verified licensed dispensary contact lists; and (4) Cannabis industry suppliers and B2B services including packaging companies (compliant child-resistant packaging, exit bags, labels), security system providers (required by most state regulations — cameras, access control, alarm systems at $10,000-$50,000 upfront plus monitoring fees), testing laboratories (legally mandated potency and contaminant testing at $50-$150 per sample batch with dispensaries testing 50-500+ batches annually = $2,500-$75,000/year testing spend), point-of-purchase displays, POS hardware (iPads, cash drawers, receipt printers, label printers), armored car services for cash transport, accounting firms specializing in IRS 280E tax compliance (cannabis businesses cannot deduct normal business expenses under federal tax code, requiring specialized CPA expertise at $5,000-$30,000/year in accounting fees), HR and payroll providers, legal compliance consultants, and marketing agencies specializing in cannabis advertising within state regulatory constraints. Smaller but extremely high-value total addressable market: approximately 15,000-20,000 licensed cannabis dispensaries and retail stores across 24 adult-use states plus 38 medical-only states as of 2026, plus 8,000-12,000 licensed cultivation facilities (indoor grows, outdoor farms, greenhouses), plus 5,000-8,000 licensed manufacturers and processors (edibles, concentrates, infused products), plus 2,000-3,000 licensed testing laboratories and distributors, for combined 30,000-43,000 total licensed cannabis businesses nationwide — smaller TAM than healthcare but MUCH higher average revenue per business ($2M-$8M annual revenue for average dispensary, $5M-$30M for large cultivation operations) and correspondingly higher willingness-to-pay for B2B services and software. Comprehensive public data availability in all legal cannabis states: California Department of Cannabis Control maintains Cannabis Unified License Search updated daily with all businesses licensed by DCC including license types (retailer, distributor, cultivator, manufacturer, testing lab, microbusiness), business names, license numbers, and license status, with bulk download capability via Higher Origins License Search tool aggregating daily-updated information on all licensed California cannabis businesses; additional state regulatory databases in Colorado MED, Washington State LCB, Oregon OLCC, Nevada CCB, Michigan CRA, Illinois IDFPR Cannabis Regulation, Massachusetts CCC, Arizona ADHS, New Jersey CRC, New York OCM, and 20+ additional adult-use and medical states all maintaining public licensing databases under state cannabis control regulations. All cannabis licensing data is 100% public under state freedom of information laws and cannabis regulatory transparency requirements — license holders, business names, license types, and license status are public records with zero privacy restrictions (cultivators may opt to protect facility addresses for security, but business entity and license status remain public). Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or API-fetch from 38 medical + 24 adult-use state cannabis control boards (California offers bulk data via third-party aggregators like Higher Origins, other states require individual record scraping), normalize license types across state-specific nomenclature (retailer vs. dispensary vs. retail store, cultivator vs. grower vs. producer, manufacturer vs. processor vs. infused product maker), deduplicate vertically integrated multi-license holders (many operators hold both retail and cultivation licenses), geocode business addresses where disclosed for location filtering, and flag license status (active, pending, suspended for regulatory violations, revoked). No affordable flat-file competitor exists below $1,000 on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing cannabis database vendors require contact for enterprise pricing quotes (typical pattern for high-value niche B2B lists), and traditional B2B data brokers charge $0.15-$0.50 per contact for cannabis industry leads (premium pricing due to niche vertical and compliance complexity), making a $149 one-time CSV deliver massive cost advantage. Score is 7 due to strong validated commercial vendor ecosystem (5+ vendors, though pricing requires quotes suggesting premium/enterprise model), exceptionally high buyer LTV across all four segments (cannabis POS software mandatory for legal operation at $3,600-$18,000/year, payment processing at $15K-$100K/year revenue per customer, insurance at $15K-$100K/year premiums with 10-15% broker commissions, specialized B2B services at $5K-$50K/year), confirmed public data availability across all legal cannabis states with California offering bulk access, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, smaller but ultra-high-value TAM (30K-43K licensed businesses with $2M-$8M average revenue creating premium B2B buyer market), and mandatory compliance software/services creating captive buyer demand. Score not higher than 7 due to: (a) public pricing not disclosed by vendors (requires enterprise sales contact, suggesting possible volume minimums or higher baseline than $149 wedge), (b) smaller TAM than healthcare verticals (30K-43K vs. 400K-700K), though partially offset by much higher revenue per business and correspondingly higher B2B buyer willingness-to-pay, and (c) potential address privacy restrictions for cultivation facilities (security concerns) though license status and business entity remain fully public.
